html:
Retatrutide is not yet approved as a medicine in Indonesia or anywhere else. As of November 2026, it is still an investigational drug in Eli Lilly’s clinical trial programme. BPOM has not registered it, and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not reviewed it yet; Lilly plans to submit its application to the FDA in the first quarter of 2027.

That does not mean you cannot find it. In Bali, retatrutide is available as a research compound, supplied for laboratory and research use rather than as a prescription medicine.

So the answer has two parts: not approved as a medicine yet, and available for research. The rest of this article explains where the drug stands in the approval process and how research supply works.

What is retatrutide?

Retatrutide is an experimental once-weekly injection developed by Eli Lilly, with the research code LY3437943. It is a GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist, which means one molecule acts on three hormone receptors involved in appetite, blood sugar and energy use.

That third receptor is what sets it apart. Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 only, and tirzepatide acts on GLP-1 and GIP. Retatrutide adds glucagon, a hormone that can raise the amount of energy the body burns.

Lilly is testing it for obesity, type 2 diabetes, knee osteoarthritis pain, obstructive sleep apnoea, and heart and kidney outcomes. We cover what retatrutide is and what the trials show in more depth in our longer guide. This article focuses on its approval status and how it is available today.

Retatrutide approval status in 2026

Retatrutide has finished the main phase 3 trials for obesity, but it has not been submitted to any regulator yet. In its August 2026 results, Lilly said the clinical data package is now complete to support global registrations for obesity, and that it plans to file a Biologics License Application with the FDA in the first quarter of 2027.

These are the phase 3 results Lilly has reported so far, newest first:

Reported Trial Who took part Headline result
October 2026 TRANSCEND-T2D-2 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes, compared with Ozempic About 2.2% A1C reduction versus 1.8% with Ozempic; 19.5% to 20.9% weight loss versus 9.4% at 80 weeks
August 2026 Three more phase 3 obesity trials Adults with obesity, with and without related conditions Positive results; Lilly called the obesity data package complete
May 2026 TRIUMPH-1 Adults with obesity and at least one weight-related condition 28.3% average weight loss on the highest dose versus 2.2% with placebo at 80 weeks
December 2025 TRIUMPH-4 Adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis Up to 28.7% weight loss at 68 weeks; more people stopped treatment because of side effects than on placebo

Strong trial results are not the same as approval. A regulator still has to review the full safety and manufacturing data, agree the approved uses, and set the label, including the dose schedule and warnings. Until that happens, there is no official dose, no approved indication and no product you can be prescribed outside a trial.

Even after an FDA decision, each country decides on its own. Indonesia would need a separate BPOM registration before retatrutide could be sold here as a medicine.

Is retatrutide approved in Indonesia?

Retatrutide does not have BPOM registration as a medicine yet. That follows from where the drug is globally: in October 2026, Lilly said retatrutide is not approved by the FDA or any other regulator, and it has not yet filed for approval anywhere.

Its current status shapes how it is available in Indonesia:

  1. It is not prescribed as a medicine. Without an approved label, there is no official indication or dose for doctors to prescribe from.
  2. Pharmacies do not stock it. Indonesian pharmacies dispense registered medicines with a BPOM number, and retatrutide does not have one yet.
  3. It is supplied as a research compound. Research suppliers provide retatrutide for laboratory and research use, labelled “research use only”.

Once Lilly applies in Indonesia and BPOM approves it, retatrutide could move from research supply to pharmacies, as tirzepatide (sold as Mounjaro) did in 2026.

Is retatrutide available in Bali?

In Bali, retatrutide is available as a research compound, not as a registered medicine. The vials sold here are labelled “for research use only”.

“Research use only” is a laboratory label. It means the product is intended for lab and research work. It has no approved dose and no approved use in people, and it is not a substitute for a prescribed medicine.

The names vary. Retatrutide is sometimes sold as “reta”, “Triple G”, “GLP-3 RT”, “GLP-3 Reta” or “GLP-3 RTA”. The “GLP-3” label is misleading: there is no GLP-3 hormone. The “3” refers to the three receptors the drug acts on, and none of these names is an official brand.

Lilly’s legal action. In August 2026, Lilly filed lawsuits against six US companies it accused of marketing research-labelled retatrutide for human use.

For research buyers, we supply retatrutide in Bali as a research compound. Our retatrutide is sold for research use only. It is not a Lilly product, it is not a BPOM-registered medicine, and it is not approved for human use.

Your options if you are interested in retatrutide

How you approach retatrutide depends on what you need it for.

  1. For laboratory research. Retatrutide is available in Bali as a research compound, supplied for research use only, as described above.
  2. For medical treatment now. Talk to a doctor. In Indonesia, tirzepatide and semaglutide are registered for weight management and type 2 diabetes, with approved dose schedules.
  3. To take part in a study. Retatrutide trials are listed on ClinicalTrials.gov, where you can search by drug name and country.
  4. To use it as a prescribed medicine. Follow the approval timeline: Lilly plans to file with the FDA in early 2027, and a BPOM decision would follow separately.

Whatever your purpose, follow the conditions the product is supplied under, and involve a doctor in any health decision.

Conclusion

Retatrutide is not yet approved as a medicine in Indonesia or elsewhere. Lilly has completed its main obesity trials and plans to file with the FDA in the first quarter of 2027, and a BPOM registration would follow separately.

The trial results explain the interest, with weight loss of around 28% on the highest dose in two phase 3 obesity studies. Until approval, retatrutide in Bali is available as a research compound, supplied for research use only and sometimes sold under names such as “reta” or “Triple G”.

For medical treatment today, talk to a doctor about the registered options, tirzepatide and semaglutide. For research, choose a supplier that labels its retatrutide clearly as research use only.

Frequently asked questions

Is retatrutide approved by the FDA?

No. As of November 2026, the FDA has not reviewed retatrutide. Lilly plans to submit its Biologics License Application in the first quarter of 2027.

Is retatrutide approved by BPOM?

No. Retatrutide does not have BPOM registration as a medicine yet. In Indonesia, it is currently available as a research compound, not as a prescription medicine.

When will retatrutide be approved?

No approval date has been announced. The FDA filing is planned for early 2027, and approval in each country depends on that country’s regulator. Indonesia would need its own BPOM decision.

Can I buy retatrutide in Bali?

Yes, as a research compound. Retatrutide in Bali is supplied for research use only. It is not sold as a prescription medicine, because it has not been approved yet.

Is “GLP-3” the same as retatrutide?

Sellers use “GLP-3” and “GLP-3 RT” as nicknames for retatrutide. The name is misleading, because there is no GLP-3 hormone. The “3” refers to the three receptors retatrutide acts on.

How is retatrutide different from tirzepatide?

Tirzepatide acts on two receptors, GIP and GLP-1, and is approved in Indonesia as Mounjaro. Retatrutide adds a third, glucagon, and is still in trials.

Who makes retatrutide?

Eli Lilly, the same company that makes tirzepatide.
